title: Backend: host-spawned launcher worker with process-tree supervision, cancel, and one run per worktree
outcome:
HOW (children: tm-ncc6.3.1 spawn+supervise, .3.2 cancel, .3.3 admission)
- Spawn the launcher in FOREGROUND mode as a hidden child of TermAl: `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs full` (or `focused -- ...`, `live --engram-binary ... --engram-sha256 ...`), cwd = project root, argument arrays only. Reuse the terminal process-tree helpers in src/terminal.rs: configure_terminal_process_tree (CREATE_SUSPENDED/setsid), TerminalProcessTree::attach + resume_after_attach (job object / process group), kill_before_reap, cleanup_after_shell_exit; stdout/stderr of the worker go to a host-side receipt log inside the run dir is NOT possible before the run dir exists, so capture stdout only until the launcher prints its receipt (run dir, manifest path, expected fingerprint - tm-uex8.12), then stop reading and let the launcher own the logs.
- Record pid + run_dir + expected_fingerprint immediately (state queued -> running) and return to the caller; a detached reaper thread waits for exit (like reap_engram_doctor_in_background in src/engram_host_adapter.rs) and then reads results.json to finalize the record (terminal state) and refresh waits (tm-ncc6.5).
- Cancel: terminate the tree (TerminalProcessTree::kill_before_reap), wait bounded, then read results.json; the launcher writes stages as failed/unrun on kill; TermAl records state canceled + reason and never writes into the launcher's files.
- Admission: one run per root: refuse (409 with the active run_id) when a non-terminal record exists for the root or execution.lock exists in a non-terminal run dir; no host queue in this slice.
- Every spawn hidden (windowsHide equivalent: CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows), tm-zdlg.

DEPENDS ON: tm-ncc6.2, tm-uex8.12 (foreground receipt printed before stages). BLOCKS: tm-ncc6.4, .5.

REVIEW FIXES (F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F9, F13)
- F1: the foreground launcher prints NOTHING until the end, then writes the whole summary (up to ~6000 chars of diagnostics + headers; launcher:718, 606-643) to stdout. Never stop reading or close the pipes: drain stdout and stderr to EOF in reader threads with a bounded capture that keeps draining after the cap (template: src/bounded_read_process.rs:46-110 run_bounded_read_process_with_setup and bounded_read_pipe 4-33; terminal.rs reader threads 560-580). The receipt (tm-uex8.12) is parsed from the live stream; the captured summary text becomes the wake body (tm-ncc6.5.2).
- F2: on kill the launcher writes nothing (no signal handler): results.json stays running/unrun. Cancel = host verdict canceled + reason, sticky; TermAl never writes into the run dir.
- F3: use a DEDICATED job object without JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE for test runs (contract option B, tm-ncc6.1) so a TermAl restart does not kill the run; Unix: setsid group (src/terminal.rs:818-878 Unix impl; Windows impl 657-694). Spawn flags: CREATE_NO_WINDOW | CREATE_SUSPENDED (precedent bounded_read_process.rs:60-65), attach, resume.
- F5: admission = no non-terminal host record for the root and no disk-indexed running results.json with a live identity-matched pid; execution.lock is not a lock for this purpose.
- F6: host-assigned run_id at spawn (state starting, pid known); launcher id / run dir / expected fingerprint filled from the receipt; the tool returns known fields after a bounded wait for the receipt and the rest via delta/get.
- F9: env TERMAL_SESSION_ID=<requester>, no --notify.
- Builder returns a plain struct {program, args, cwd, env, creation_flags} so flags are unit-testable; fixtures: src/tests/fixtures/test-launcher-receipt-fixture.mjs (prints the receipt line, spawns a grandchild, writes results.json, then exits) with a long-stdout variant.

DEPENDS ON: tm-ncc6.1 (decisions A/B), tm-ncc6.2, tm-uex8.12 (parseable receipt before stages).

OUTPUT TO FILE (Greg, 2026-09-23): NO PIPES. Greg's objection to option B: pipes belong to the TermAl instance that spawned the worker; after a restart nothing can read them, so any output read only through pipes (receipt, final summary) is lost, and the drain-to-EOF requirement (F1) exists only because of pipes. Decision: the host opens a per-run file it owns BEFORE spawning - HOST_LOG = <review-runs>/host/<host_run_id>.launcher.log (review-runs resolved as the launcher does; the run dir does not exist yet at spawn time) - and passes it as the child's stdout AND stderr (stdin null). No pipe is ever created. The receipt (tm-uex8.12) is read by tailing HOST_LOG with a bounded wait; the final summary is read from HOST_LOG after exit (or after re-attach). Progress never depended on pipes: the launcher writes each stage's stdout/stderr straight to <runDir>/<stage>.log (scripts/test-launcher.mjs runCommand, ~247-266) and stage states to results.json at stage boundaries, so the log stream (tm-ncc6.6) and the UI (tm-ncc6.7) show live progress before and after a restart. F1's 'drain to EOF' requirement is replaced by 'no pipes'; the record stores host_log_path.
acceptance:
- Start returns run_id at once and run_dir/expected fingerprint after the receipt is read from HOST_LOG; no stage runs before the receipt is written (fixture asserts order).
- The child has no pipes: a fixture whose final stdout exceeds 64 KiB exits normally and its summary is fully present in HOST_LOG; the record finalizes from results.json.
- Cancel terminates the whole tree on Windows (job object) and Unix (process group): a fixture grandchild is gone; results.json stays non-terminal (killed stage running, later stages unrun) and the record is canceled with the reason; never passed.
- A worker that exits with terminal results is adopted as passed/failed exactly once (reaper), also when boot reconciliation runs concurrently.
- Second start for the same root while one is active -> 409 naming the active run_id; a dead-pid unknown run does not block.
- Creation flags asserted on the builder struct; on Windows a fixture asserts GetConsoleWindow() == 0 in the child.
- Progress across a simulated restart: while a fixture stage is still writing its stage log, dropping and re-creating the supervisor (tm-ncc6.3.4) does not stop the stage log from growing, and the tail route keeps serving it.
